pr_snapshot.body:
VP8 ARM filtering still runs the correction arithmetic and identity stores when every lane's rounded correction is zero. Skip that work for macroblock `|f|≤2` and internal `|f|≤3`, preserving carried pixels and later-edge evaluation. Keep larger corrections active, including signed `-128`. Generate the ARM checks from the existing canonical network; AMD production output stays byte-identical.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go 1.27.2 SIMD, PGO off, six fresh permutations with identical public-call fixtures and scalar output checks:

- Flat/gradient tiles improve **1.806–1.843× versus main**, all 24 paired results at least **1.770×**, zero allocations.
- The same cases improve **1.636–1.658× versus ARM assembly**; every pair is faster.
- Gradient tiles also improve **1.605–1.610× versus the zero-only design**, with all 12 pairs at least 1.562×. Preserve both designs' complete evidence.
- Other textured/noop controls range 0.991–1.007× main; keep every slower result. Active textured cases still trail assembly by about 9.7–10.6%.

- 300-frame720p: +0.606% encode time versus main (2/6 faster), +8.354% versus assembly.
- 60-frame720p: +1.042% encode time versus main (1/6 faster), +12.340% versus assembly.

All23 non-timing result fields match in every whole sample and allocations stay zero. The assembly gap remains open; component gains are reported separately.

Retain the correctness-verified component wins under AGENTS.md independently of whole-codec timing. Validation includes the full native Go suite, scalar filter oracles, 640 boundary/alignment/late-edge cases, race/checkptr2, six fixed-speed packet/drop digest comparisons, independent numeric/generator review, and regenerated PGO/fingerprint/noasm/build-selection/precommit checks. The generated hot source matches the timed candidate byte-for-byte.

Expand identical native AMD fixtures from 154 to 158 cases so flat/gradient controls are measured on the same host against assembly/main/current. Native AMD and optimized-libvpx jobs provide the new PR's controls. Preserve PR32's complete 160-file native/C audit separately: EPYC 9V74 x4 full scans 3.097–3.135× main and 35–39% less time than assembly; whole VP8 still 11.196% slower than assembly; separate fixed VP8 takes 2.315× optimized libvpx time at matching measured quality/payload/counts.

Archive all raw samples, source variants, hashes, correctness/codegen evidence and unselected ARM probes outside README. README and dependencies unchanged.

Fresh native x64 CI controls, EPYC 7763, Go 1.27.2, PGO off, six paired rounds versus main `20bc81cb` and old assembly `691cd051`:
- AMD generated production source remains byte-identical (SHA256 `b69d744831c843e19ca85dee962d37da3f5e43bbd82413f221fb4a4ad5f79e67`); this is generated-source identity, not a newly compiled-code claim. Treat every AMD timing difference as a control.
- Whole VP8 -0.093% time versus main, VP9 320 -0.064%, VP9 720 +0.308%; each has 3/6 faster pairs. On this CPU they take 14.172%/39.394%/46.772% less time than assembly respectively. These controls do not close previously observed gaps on ARM or other x64 CPUs.
- The four new flat/ramp controls range -2.050% to +0.365% versus main and remain 18.674–21.253% slower than assembly. All 10 picker fixtures compare the complete public result against separate original edge operations in each variant; no AMD assembly case is excluded.
- All 158 kernel cases have six samples per variant and zero B/op/allocs. Targeted validation passes 78 top-level tests plus six retained panic child probes (84 checks; 106 PASS lines including older subtests), no failures/skips, with main/current SIMD dispatch confirmed. All 22 semantic fields match across three public and two profile datasets. Every allocation sample matches; no outliers this run.
- Preserve all 54 median-regressing kernels. Sole all-six-slower control: VP9 FPClasses 8x8/zero +0.131%. Remaining measured assembly gaps include SixTap4x4 phases +203.9–249.1%, residual gather8/16 +138.5%/+129.8%, and quantizer batch2 +120.9%. In the separate 2.36s current VP8 profile, loopFilterBytes records 0.12s flat/0.48s cumulative, forwardDCT4BatchGo 0.08s/0.10s and QuantizeVP8Batch 0.05s/0.09s. These short-profile samples identify investigation targets; cumulative samples overlap and do not establish isolated throughput ratios.

Separate optimized-C job on Intel Xeon 6973P-C: pinned libvpx v1.16.0 with runtime dispatch, SSE2/AVX2 and assembly objects enabled. Fixed-speed VP8 uses 2.229x libvpx time (+122.853%) with matching measured PSNR/SSIM/payload/encoded and dropped counts; this does not assert bitstream identity. Adaptive VP8 +68.286%, VP9 +183.852%/+202.888% use unequal quality/output work. Every quality-pass output statistic matches timed output; reference timing uses vpxenc statistics. Do not infer source effects or compare absolute timings across separate jobs.

All three exact-head CI checks pass. Raw artifacts: [native](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39068461294/artifacts/12114623465), [optimized C](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39068461294/artifacts/12114511707).
